The social issue

Sign language is a Deaf person’s first and only native language.

Yet it has long been denied — even mocked as te-mane 手真似, “monkey imitation.”

When no one can interpret

Deaf people are turned away from help everyone else takes for granted.

Banking

Instead of providing translation, a bank refused to let a Deaf customer open an account alone.

Source: DPI Japan, via Japan’s FSA (2026)

Police · Yokohama

Yokohama police refused to take a statement from a Deaf person.

Source: City of Yokohama · 障害者差別事例 17

From our interviews

Deaf taxi driver Mr. Ong was assaulted while signing. Police refused to provide an interpreter, and he was intimidated into dropping his report.

Source: New Straits Times, 23 July 2026

A two-way sign language interpreter in your pocket.

How it works

One conversation. Both directions.

Deaf signer kotoSay Hearing person

Impact

Communicate autonomously, in the moments that shape a life.

Education

Ask questions and take part in class, in your own sign language.

Banking

Built to address concerns raised by the WFD and WASLI, kotoSay unlocks career and personal independence.

WFD: World Federation of the Deaf · WASLI: World Association of Sign Language Interpreters

Validation

Tested, refined and validated with the Deaf community.

  1. 1 Test

    Evaluated with 8 MSL researchers at UKM. They found limits with fast and distant signs.

  2. 2 Refine

    Refined the model to reach a 1.5 m functional range during rapid signing.

  3. 3 Validate

    A Deaf worker at the RC Deaf Missions (RCDM) café praised its faster speed, instant voice and expanded range.

What’s next

RCDM’s co-founder expressed strong interest in a long-term co-creation partnership to grow kotoSay into a Relay Interpreting Services platform.

Business model

A B2B / B2C subscription for users, families and employers.

¥190/ month

after a 2-month free trial

  1. 1

    Instant, on demand

    Free interpreters require rigid advance booking. kotoSay gives real-time access whenever it’s needed.

  2. 2

    Easier hiring compliance

    Helps companies meet Japan’s 2.7% disability hiring quota.

  3. 3

    Healthy unit economics

    Serving even heavy users costs under ¥100 a month, for a ~47% profit margin.

Growth strategy

From 2 sign languages to 11, and from an app to a platform.

  1. Phase 1 · Q3 2027

    Grow and pilot

    • Expand vocabulary to 300+ JSL / MSL signs
    • Launch pilots with regional Deaf associations
    • Incorporate and secure institutional growth capital
  2. Phase 2 · Q4 2028

    Open the platform

    • Launch a pay-as-you-go API
    • Banks, clinics and taxis integrate kotoSay natively
  3. Phase 3 · Q1 2030

    Scale across Asia

    • Train our core ML pipeline across 11 Asian sign languages
